label.justification: The obligation is over one carrier, the SUPER_PERMISSIONED init bond that the factory forwards as msg.value, and two edges that both judge it: the U20 configuration validator, which accepts only zero, and the pre-fix payable SuperPermissionedDisputeGame.initialize, which accepts any value. The witness is the test's setInitBond(SUPER_PERMISSIONED, 1 ether): the validator rejects this bond, but the game accepts it and creates a clone holding the ETH. SORT's obligation is not falsified, even though it names fewer components: the ETH is not underflowed, truncated, mis-typed or destroyed, and it stays conserved in the clone's balance, only stranded. So the conservation reading does not apply, and the tie order is never reached. DISCH fits only secondarily: the stranded ETH has no withdrawal guard at all, so its obligation would need a closure over the clone's whole exit surface, which names more components. The fix adds the zero-value check to the game itself, which brings the two acceptance paths back into agreement.
label.subform: acceptance checks that differ between components (config validator vs game initializer)

label.justification: The obligation is over one interface carrier, the sequencer message, and its decoders: readerForBlobReader.recoverInternal (slicing at offset 41) and recoverPayloadFromBatchInternal (slicing at offset 40). Every decoder of that carrier must accept the same inputs. The witness is a message shorter than the fixed header. The path that posts or dispatches the batch lets it through, but these decoders slice past its end and crash the node instead of rejecting it, as the source says. This matches the sheet's PAR typical defect exactly ('length or version checks that differ between components'). SORT would be smaller, but its obligation covers sign or width wraps, truncations that change meaning, union-member confusion and conservation; a slice beyond the buffer that panics changes no value's sort, so SORT is not clearly falsified and is kept only as a secondary reading.
label.subform: decoder domain coherence: a length check present on one path to the sequencer-message decoders and absent on another
